The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 92 from Joshua Silva, complemented by a commanding 118-run stand between AS Joseph and Joshua Silva that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.87 RPO. Bangladesh's bowling response was spearheaded by Abu Jayed (4/98), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Finishing at 409/10 (142.2 ov), West Indies established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Shere Bangla National Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 409/10 (142.2 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Bangladesh countered with 296/10 (96.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 106 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Taijul Islam delivered a masterclass for Bangladesh (21 Runs & 8 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (West Indies 45%) and allowing West Indies to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. West Indies's bowling unit, bolstered by RRS Cornwall (5 Runs & 9 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing West Indies won by 17 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: West Indies's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, West Indies won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
